% -------------------------------------------------
% Abstract
% -------------------------------------------------
\begin{abstract}
    FlashLock is a simple Spring Boot application demonstrating a basic order management system. It provides RESTful APIs for CRUD operations on products and orders, utilizes an in‑memory H2 database for rapid prototyping, and follows a clean layered architecture (controller, service, repository). This report documents the system design, implementation details, testing strategy, and usage instructions.
\end{abstract}
\clearpage

% -------------------------------------------------
% Introduction
% -------------------------------------------------
\chapter{Introduction}
\section{Motivation}
The need for lightweight, quickly deployable back‑end services is common in teaching, prototypes, and small‑scale applications. FlashLock showcases how Spring Boot can be leveraged to build a maintainable REST API with minimal configuration.

\section{Objectives}
\begin{itemize}[noitemsep]
    \item Implement CRUD operations for products and orders.
    \item Use Spring Data JPA with an H2 in‑memory database.
    \item Provide global exception handling and basic validation.
    \item Offer a clear, documented code base for educational purposes.
\end{itemize}

% -------------------------------------------------
% System Architecture
% -------------------------------------------------
\chapter{System Architecture}
\section{High‑Level Overview}
The application follows a classic three‑layer architecture:
\begin{enumerate}[noitemsep]
    \item \textbf{Presentation Layer}: Spring MVC RestControllers expose HTTP endpoints.
    \item \textbf{Business Layer}: Service classes contain the core logic.
    \item \textbf{Persistence Layer}: Spring Data JPA repositories interact with the H2 database.
\end{enumerate}

% Implementation Details

\chapter{Implementation Details}
\section{Technology Stack}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
    \toprule
    Category & Technology \\ \midrule
    Language & Java 17 \\
    Framework & Spring Boot 3.x \\
    Build Tool & Maven Wrapper (./mvnw) \\
    Database & H2 (in‑memory) \\
    Testing & JUnit 5, Spring Boot Test \\
    Version Control & Git (GitHub) \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\section{Key Classes}
\begin{itemize}[noitemsep]
    \item \texttt{FlashLockApplication.java}: Main entry point.
    \item \texttt{Product.java}, \texttt{Order.java}: Entity models.
    \item \texttt{ProductRepository}, \texttt{OrderRepository}: JPA repositories.
    \item \texttt{ProductController}, \texttt{OrderController}: REST controllers.
    \item \texttt{ProductService}, \texttt{OrderService}: Business logic.
    \item \texttt{GlobalExceptionHandler.java}: Centralised error handling.
    \item \texttt{SecurityConfig.java}: Placeholder for future security configuration.
\end{itemize}

\section{Configuration}
The application uses \texttt{application.properties} to configure the H2 console and logging. Sample snippet:
\begin{verbatim}
spring.h2.console.enabled=true
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:flashlockdb
spring.datasource.driverClassName=org.h2.Driver
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
\end{verbatim}

% -------------------------------------------------
% Testing Strategy
% -------------------------------------------------
\chapter{Testing Strategy}
Unit tests are placed under \texttt{src/test/java}. Example test for \texttt{OrderService} verifies order creation and retrieval. Integration tests use \texttt{@SpringBootTest} to start the full application context.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Results and Discussion
% -------------------------------------------------
\chapter{Results and Discussion}
The system compiles and runs with a single command:
\begin{verbatim}
./mvnw spring-boot:run
\end{verbatim}
All REST endpoints respond correctly (see Section~\ref{sec:api}). The in‑memory H2 database makes it trivial to reset state between runs. Performance benchmarks are not required for this prototype.

% -------------------------------------------------
% API Documentation
% -------------------------------------------------
\section{API Endpoints}\label{sec:api}
\begin{tabular}{p{3cm} p{5cm} p{5cm}}
    \toprule
    Method & URL & Description \\
    \midrule
    GET & /api/products & Retrieve all products \\
    POST & /api/products & Create a new product \\
    GET & /api/products/{id} & Get product by ID \\
    PUT & /api/products/{id} & Update existing product \\
    DELETE & /api/products/{id} & Delete product \\
    GET & /api/orders & Retrieve all orders \\
    POST & /api/orders & Create a new order \\
    GET & /api/orders/{id} & Get order by ID \\
    PUT & /api/orders/{id} & Update existing order \\
    DELETE & /api/orders/{id} & Delete order \\
    \bottomrule
\end{tabular}

% -------------------------------------------------
% Conclusion
% -------------------------------------------------
\chapter{Conclusion}
FlashLock demonstrates how quickly a functional REST API can be built using Spring Boot with minimal configuration. The project serves as a teaching aid for newcomers to Java back‑end development and can be extended with authentication, persistence to a external DB, and front‑end integration.
